item.title: Bugzy Malone Envisions Life Beyond Rap
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Bugzy Malone outlined plans for more music beyond his rapper role, alongside an expanding film and television career.
item.content:encoded:
Bugzy Malone pictured a future in which he keeps making music but leaves the rapper role behind, with a TV role in The Gentlemen now on his slate.

In his Modern Wisdom interview, released November 9, he tied that shift to a future second part of Make It Maintain It, Pt. 1.

“I’ll make it and I won’t be promoting it as a rapper because I won’t be a rapper at that point,” he said.

He linked rap to youth and the climb out of a hard life. He expected to be a husband and father by then, whether or not his acting career had taken off. The plan still includes a record for fans who follow his work, though he gave no date for that next stage.

The new TV role builds on his work with Guy Ritchie. His casting in the third season of Netflix’s The Gentlemen was announced on October 23. The crime series was filmed in Britain and Morocco, so his place in the cast was public before the latest interview came out.

He is among the actors playing new characters in the series. The casting announcement did not name his role or give a date for the new season to reach viewers.

His plans for work beyond rap have already changed the way he spends his time. In 2021, Bugzy called his UK headline tour his last as film jobs and his clothing and footwear brands took up more of his schedule.

He marked that step with The Night We Made History, a documentary about the buildup to the final tour date. The tour included a sold-out show at the arena in his hometown of Manchester.

By 2023, his push into film had grown beyond an ambition. He had appeared in The Gentlemen and the spy thriller Operation Fortune: Ruse de Guerre, both directed by Ritchie. He also looked back at his 2019 plans to reach Hollywood, setting that earlier goal against the screen work he had since done.

In the new interview, Bugzy said he had shaved his head as part of his focus on acting.

item.title: Birdman Beats Lil Wayne Tour Bus Driver's Lawsuit
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Birdman and Cash Money leave the long-running civil case after a Georgia judge rejects the driver's evidence against them.
item.content:encoded:
Birdman no longer has to defend himself against a driver’s decade-old lawsuit over the shooting of Lil Wayne’s tour bus. A Georgia judge dismissed him and Cash Money Records from the case Tuesday.

The ruling comes down to evidence connecting the defendants to the 2015 attack. According to TMZ’s report on the order, the judge found that Birdman wasn’t in Georgia that night.

The judge also found that driver Alvin Lewis failed to “identify any admissible evidence that Bryan Williams or Cash Money Records were involved in the bus shooting,” TMZ reported.

Lewis has spent years seeking compensation for what he says the shooting cost him. His lawsuit alleged the attack left him fearing for his life and caused continuing physical and emotional injuries, along with lost wages.

The judge noted that neither bullets nor shrapnel struck Lewis. The driver nevertheless maintained that the experience caused lasting harm, making his claims about injuries part of the civil dispute.

The case was still drawing courtroom arguments this summer. AllHipHop previously reported on Young Thug’s attorneys challenging the tour bus lawsuit during an August appearance in Cobb County.

That hearing concerned allegations that Young Thug and Birdman arranged the attack after Wayne left an Atlanta concert.

Those were Lewis’s allegations, and Tuesday’s reported decision removes Birdman and Cash Money from his pursuit of damages.

Lewis brought claims including assault and battery, breach of contract and intentional infliction of emotional distress. He filed the lawsuit about ten years ago, following the 2015 shooting.

The judge directed the court clerk to remove Birdman and Cash Money Records as defendants.

item.title: Keefe D Gets 120-Day Deadline In Tupac Murder Appeal
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Keefe D's appeal enters its next stage in Nevada as his legal team faces a briefing deadline after Michael Sanft's death.
item.content:encoded:
Keefe D now has a deadline to challenge his Tupac Shakur murder conviction after losing the attorney who took him through trial.

The Nevada Supreme Court has docketed the appeal and ordered his attorneys to submit their opening brief within 120 days, according to KTNV.

The case moves into that next stage with a 40-years-to-life sentence hanging over the 63-year-old. Judge Carli Kierny handed down the punishment on October 13 after jurors convicted him of first-degree murder with use of a deadly weapon.

His defense now faces the loss of Michael Sanft, whose death was reported November 6 after he represented Keefe D during the trial.

Sanft had already made clear that the defense intended to challenge the guilty verdict rather than let the sentencing end its fight.

At trial, the prosecution put Keefe D in the group seeking retaliation after Tupac and his associates fought his nephew Orlando Anderson. Prosecutors argued that he obtained the gun used in the shooting, building their case around his recorded accounts and public statements.

The defense challenged whether those accounts could be trusted, arguing that stories told in interviews and a memoir were exaggerated for money.

Jurors also heard evidence beyond those statements, including surveillance footage of the MGM Grand fight and testimony about his documentary interviews.

Keefe D didn’t testify during the trial, leaving jurors to weigh his earlier words instead of hearing him answer questions on the stand. They returned their verdict on August 31 after less than three hours of deliberations.

The appeal follows a prosecution over the September 7, 1996, shooting near the Las Vegas Strip while Tupac rode with Suge Knight. Tupac died six days later at age 25, leaving a case that remained without charges for decades.

Police arrested Keefe D in September 2023, nearly 27 years after the fatal shooting.

item.title: Wiz Khalifa Takes Unreleased Music To Diplo’s Finish Line
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Wiz Khalifa pairs a Los Angeles race appearance with a Diplo stage surprise as new tracks enter the Run Club rollout.
item.content:encoded:
Wiz Khalifa gave runners more than a finish-line celebration when he joined Diplo onstage to tease unreleased music in Los Angeles.

The rapper ran the November 8 race before making his surprise appearance, according to Diplo’s announcement through Sacks & Co.

“This song has been in my head for a long time, it’s an anthem that helps me do hard things,” said Diplo. “It gets me out of bed and on a run when I don’t have a lot of gas in the tank. It reminds me how far I’ve come and how bright I know the future will be despite the daily struggles we all face. I hope it motivates my fans and the community we’ve created with Diplo’s Run Club to keep showing up.”

The sold-out event brought the producer’s Run Club back to Los Angeles State Historic Park for a morning built around miles and music. Its advertised course stretched through Chinatown and past the Los Angeles River before the post-race concert brought everyone back together.

Wiz’s appearance adds another rapper to a rollout that’s turning Diplo’s races into listening sessions for an upcoming companion project. A$AP Ferg already joined him in New York, while San Francisco got unreleased music featuring Too $hort and Kah-Lo.

Diplo also previewed Keep Your Head Up in Los Angeles before releasing the song November 9. “This song has been in my head for a long time, it’s an anthem that helps me do hard things,” Diplo said in his supplied statement.

Diplo has been recording with longtime collaborators to put together tracks aimed at runners and athletes. Some of that music is already available in an exclusive mix that race participants can access through the location-based Echoes app at Run Club events.

The Los Angeles schedule put the race start at 9 A.M. and Diplo’s set at 11 A.M., leaving the party for after the workout.

Participants’ registration included festival admission alongside their race entry, shirt and finisher medal, so the music was built into the day’s plans.

For Wiz, the appearance comes as he’s building on a return to Warner through 10K Projects and another round of RIAA certifications. His singles Black and Yellow and Young, Wild & Free with Snoop Dogg both reached Diamond status last month.

The new deal also reunites Wiz with 10K Projects president Marsha St. Hubert, who worked on his breakthrough album Rolling Papers. That 2011 release carried Black and Yellow alongside Roll Up and No Sleep, linking his latest move to those early hits.

Diplo’s Run Club next reaches Gallagher Square at San Diego’s Petco Park on November 21.

item.title: Pooh Shiesty Gets New Jail Agreement In Gucci Mane Kidnapping Case
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Lawyers for Pooh Shiesty agreed to seek a new jail after a fight over isolation while his Gucci Mane case heads to trial.
item.content:encoded:
Pooh Shiesty could be headed to another Texas jail after weeks of complaints about the isolation he’s facing while awaiting trial in the Gucci Mane kidnapping case.

Lawyers on both sides have agreed to look for a different facility.

The agreement emerged at a Tuesday hearing over his conditions of confinement, according to CBS News Texas.

The judge didn’t have to settle that dispute because prosecutors and defense attorneys agreed to work together on finding another placement.

The Memphis rapper is being held at the Rolling Plains facility in Haskell, where his attorneys have challenged the terms of his detention.

His attorneys said in October filings that he spent about 23 hours a day alone and had sharply limited family visits.

His aunt described the toll in a court letter that CBS cited: “He’s worn down, extremely anxious and seems severely depressed from being locked in a small room for most of the day, every day, with only two hours per month to see a family member in person.”

Prosecutors disputed that account, saying separate housing protected him after other inmates tried to reach him for an autograph.

As AllHipHop previously reported, they also cited more than 12,000 emails and about 230 video calls while opposing his emergency request for better treatment.

The government pointed to tablet access as another way he could communicate and pass time.

That fight over jail conditions is separate from the allegations that put him behind bars. Federal prosecutors charged nine men, including Pooh Shiesty and Big30, over an alleged January 10 armed confrontation at a Dallas recording studio.

They alleged Pooh Shiesty used an AK-style pistol to force a victim to sign paperwork releasing him from a recording contract.

Other defendants allegedly took jewelry, watches and cash while the victims were prevented from leaving. Pooh Shiesty has pleaded not guilty, and Tuesday’s agreement concerns another detention facility rather than release from custody. CBS didn’t identify a new jail or a date for the move.

AllHipHop previously reported that his trial was set for February 22, 2027, with a final pretrial conference scheduled for February 17.

item.title: Da Brat Has Message For Chicago Rappers Looking To Make It Out Of The City
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Da Brat turns her Chicago return into encouragement for aspiring rappers as she takes on a new role in a holiday production.
item.content:encoded:
Da Brat is bringing a message to a new generation of Chicago rappers as she prepares to return home this month. She’s joining The Hip Hop Nutcracker with advice for artists still trying to turn neighborhood recognition into something bigger.

“I just wanted to be a star outside of Chicago,” Da Brat told the Chicago Defender in a new interview. She remembers watching performers around the city before her own records reached listeners far beyond home.

That jump arrived with Funkdafied in 1994, when she became the first solo female rapper to earn a platinum album. Working with Jermaine Dupri and So So Def helped turn that ambition into a career that still brings her onto new stages.

She’s now taking the host and MC role in a production that pairs Hip-Hop dancing with Tchaikovsky’s familiar holiday score. The Chicago engagement brings her to the Cadillac Palace Theatre from November 24 through November 29, giving that advice a hometown audience.

“We all started from the mud and didn’t have anything. Anything is possible,” Da Brat said, encouraging younger artists to stick with their goals.

She also urged them to stay humble while putting in the work to get where they want.

Her musical education started well before the recording studio, with church giving her room to sing and play instruments. Writing poems eventually gave her another way into music, while watching other Chicago performers helped her imagine making that move herself.

The holiday show gives her a different setting from a conventional rap concert, with a dozen dancers sharing the production.

A live violinist and DJ help carry the music as the story shifts into a contemporary New York City setting. Digital graffiti replaces the familiar old-world backdrop as the characters travel through the updated version of the story.

Maria-Clara and the Nutcracker Prince remain part of the adventure, with Jennifer Weber directing and choreographing the production. The performance runs approximately two hours with an intermission and welcomes audiences of all ages to its holiday run.

Da Brat’s first Chicago performance with the production is scheduled for 7 p.m. on November 24.

item.title: EXCLUSIVE: Gamma Gets Small Win In French Montana & Ye’s “Where They At” Sample Suit
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Gamma was dropped from the French Montana and Ye sample case without prejudice, leaving room for the claim to return.
item.content:encoded:
Music firm Gamma was dropped from a suit over a clip of Ye‘s rant on French Montana‘s “Where They At.”

The claim came from photo firm Bauer-Griffin, which said it owns the rights to the video used in the song. On November 9, it filed a notice to drop Gamma from the case in federal court in Los Angeles.

Plaintiff Bauer-Griffin voluntarily dismissed Gamma without prejudice, the notice read.

That leaves room for the firm to sue Gamma again, subject to other legal limits. The notice gave no reason for the move or terms of a deal.

The rule it used lets the filing party withdraw the suit without a court order. That route applies before the other side serves an answer or asks for a ruling on the evidence without a trial.

The suit first reached court in July.

At its heart was a 45-second video filmed in May 2013 outside a Los Angeles restaurant. Bauer-Griffin said it owned the clip of Ye’s clash with a cameraman.

Its claim focused on the audio from the first part of the video, which showed Ye shouting at the man with the camera. The firm said that sound made up about the first eight seconds of the track.

Ye and Westside Gunn joined French Montana on “Where They At,” part of Mac & Cheese 5. The project came out on February 23, 2024, through Coke Boys Records under an exclusive license to Gamma.

In its July suit, Gamma accused Vydia, a music distribution firm it owns, of sending the song to streaming sites. The claim named the two firms and two producers as copying or sharing the sound.

The claim against French Montana and Ye was based on their alleged power to control that use. Bauer-Griffin said they let it proceed and profited from it.

The firm asked the court to stop further use of the clip and sought money for its losses, plus profits tied to that use.

item.title: Cardi B Joins GTA Festival
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Travis Scott and Cardi B joined GTA VI's Miami launch festival as Rockstar set November ticket lottery deadlines.
item.content:encoded:
Travis Scott and Cardi B will bring GTA VI’s music to Miami on November 21 for a two-stage festival at Mana Wynwood, two days after the game’s launch.

Scott, Don Toliver, Kodak Black and SoFaygo share the Cactus Jack Presents bill. Metro Boomin joins them, while Justice will play a DJ set. Rockstar Games has teamed with PlayStation and the crew behind III Points for the show.

For Scott and Cardi, the link starts with new songs made for the game. His track “RHYNO” and her song “Don’t Chart” are part of Grand Theft Auto VI: The Album. Both tracks are out now.

The 34-track set is due November 19, the same day as the game. Fans will have two days to hear it before the show.

Justice brings a second strand of the game’s sound to the bill. The French duo wrote the score, which shifts with how each player moves through the game.

Their own score album is due December 11, with 30 tracks plus digital bonus songs. Rockstar Games released this launch trailer on October 15, 2026.

The game’s radio hosts bring more of Miami’s roots to its world. Trick Daddy and Trina helm Dirty South Classics, which plays rap from across the South. They made the pairing public on October 8. Vice City is the game’s take on Miami, set within the wider state of Leonida.

Kodak has a place in that world, too. He confirmed he appears in the game after fans saw his likeness in a new set of images. Rockstar shared them on November 5.

His face tattoos and 1800 Block chain helped fans spot him, though details of the role are still under wraps.

Fans who want to see the live show must enter a draw by November 10 at 4 P.M. ET. They will draw names at 7 P.M. ET. Winners can buy up to two tickets the next day at noon ET.

The show is for guests 17 and up.

item.title: Zamaera and Samad Savage Bet on Themselves With Hard-Hitting Single “Xperience”
item.dc:creator: Brxton Lee
item.description: Zamaera and Samad Savage turn ambition, pressure and hard-earned resilience into “Xperience,” an explosive trap collaboration connecting Malaysian and American hip-hop.
item.content:encoded:
Every rapper has a motto. Few of them come with a warning label.

“You’re losing a hundred percent of the shots you don’t take, so when you take it better not miss.” That’s the bar at the center of “Xperience,” the new single from Malaysian independent star Zamaera and American rapper-producer Samad Savage. Half of it is motivation. The other half is a threat.

The track dropped Friday, November 6, 2026, on Mean Malaya Entertainment. It’s the second time these two have linked up, and this one goes straight for the throat.

Savage made the beat himself, and he didn’t make it pretty. It’s aggressive, high-energy trap that sets the tone before anyone says a word. Zamaera goes first, and she doesn’t open with a flex. She opens with a panic attack. She wakes up from a bad dream with her future looking nothing like she pictured, sweating and holding on to the only things she controls: her mind and her breath.

From there it’s a crash course in what ambition costs. She cuts the wasted time, then cuts the people, and admits the ones she dropped were the closest to her. She calls the road a marathon. Then she drops a bar that belongs on every young artist’s wall: “If you live by praise then you’ll die by the diss.” Everybody raps about blocking out the haters. Not many admit the cheering can take you out too.

Savage answers with a perfect mirror. She woke from a bad dream; he wakes up “from a good nap,” because sleeping on the competition is what he does best. He brings the jokes and the flexes, from eight-pack energy to an A$AP Mob shoutout. The realest part is his backstory. As a kid, rapping was his only escape from “the loneliest place,” so every win now goes right in your face.

The hook is where it all clicks. It runs from having no experience to visions of millions and a house in the Carbon Canyons, then lands on the title’s double meaning: living what everybody else only wants to experience. The pre-chorus keeps it simple. They came from the bottom, broke more times than they can count, and survived. Under pressure, diamonds shine.

The connection goes back to 2023 and “Kill My Vibe,” a track the two built without ever being in the same room. For a couple of years that’s how it stayed: two artists on opposite sides of the world, trading ideas across time zones.

In 2025 they finally met face to face, and they got straight to work. “Xperience” started from nothing in New York City. It went through version after version, and it wasn’t finished until 2026, when they shared a stage at SXSW in Austin, Texas. They took the energy from that show back into the song and closed it out.

Three years from the first collab to this one. In an era of songs made in an afternoon and forgotten in a week, that kind of patience says a lot.

If anybody has earned the right to rap about betting on yourself, it’s Zamaera. She’s a rapper, singer and songwriter who mixes hip-hop with electronic sounds, and she’s done it all independently. She even built her own label, Mean Malaya Entertainment, to push Malaysian talent and connect it with creative scenes around the world.

Her 2026 has been big. At SXSW she created the Made in Malaysia stage and brought five Malaysian acts to Austin, and the showcase is already locked in to return in 2027. In August she showed up on “So Much To Say” from TroyBoi’s FT EP. That led to stage time with him at Breakaway Festival in Charlotte, Global Dance Festival in Denver, Brownies & Lemonade in Los Angeles and EDC Korea 2026.

Then came September. Zamaera performed at Rick Ross’s Rap Arena in Miami, and she was the only international artist on the lineup. A Malaysian indie rapper on a Rick Ross stage, repping her country by herself. Moments like that don’t happen by accident. She went and got it.

Samad Savage brings the same energy from the other side of the world. The American rapper and producer has built his whole career himself. He makes the beats, writes the verses and keeps full control of the vision. His music deals with real life, resilience and saying exactly what he means.

You can trace that through his catalogue, from The Grey Area to Trust the Weird Kids to Duo-Litty. On “Xperience” he handles the beat and a verse, then passes the mic back to Zamaera, and the song circles back to her opening lines. When the guy telling you to control your future also built the beat you’re hearing, you believe him.

Hip-hop has always belonged to people who refused to wait their turn. Today that crowd includes a rapper from Malaysia who builds her own stages and a producer from the States who builds his own beats. They don’t share a city or a scene. What they share is a work ethic.

“Xperience” is what you get when two people like that meet halfway around the world and decide to say it plainly. Take the shot, and don’t miss.

“Xperience” by Zamaera and Samad Savage is out now on all digital streaming and download platforms worldwide via Mean Malaya Entertainment.

item.title: Coolio Comes Back To Life In Dheezy’s Space-Themed Video
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Coolio joins Dheezy on screen through archival footage as the Australian rapper rolls out a collaboration years in the making.
item.content:encoded:
Coolio is coming back to life onscreen through a collaboration with Australian rapper Dheezy built from previously unreleased footage.

Dheezy’s team says it worked closely with the late rapper’s estate to assemble the “Shoot For The Moon” video.

The production combines archival green-screen footage with new performances inside a space-themed setting. M-Strange produced the song, which closes Dheezy Does It LP after four years of sessions between Australia and Los Angeles.

“Dheezy Does It LP is more than an album—it’s the culmination of years of hard work, sacrifice, and a lifelong love for Hip-Hop,” Dheezy told AllHipHop in a statement.

The album also includes contributions from the late rappers Nate Dogg, Proof and Chino XL.

For Coolio’s appearance, the production team matched camera angles and lighting before building the surroundings with 3D effects. Those steps allowed footage recorded during his lifetime to share the screen with Dheezy’s performance.

Snoop Dogg, Kurupt, E-40 and Planet Asia appear elsewhere on the album alongside Onyx and Big Twins.

Dheezy’s team describes Eminem as his biggest musical influence, with several guests connected to the Detroit rapper’s circle.

“This project brings together artists and influences that helped shape my journey, and I’m proud to finally share it with the world,” Dheezy said. Those connections were already taking shape before he brought this album together.

Dheezy teamed with Bizarre for the six-track Killah Kombo EP in 2023, with Kuniva and Swifty McVay also involved.

That project included “Flip Em All The Bird,” bringing his D12 collaborations into an earlier music video. That earlier EP also included Obie Trice and production from K.E. on the Track.

Coolio died in September 2022 at 59, but recordings he made during his lifetime have continued reaching listeners. The posthumous “A Star Is Born” with Treach and DJ Wino followed in 2023, adding another collaboration to his catalog.

His career stretched from “Fantastic Voyage” to “C U When U Get There,” with “Gangsta’s Paradise” becoming his biggest crossover hit. The Dheezy video gives another archived performance a place in a new release.

KXNG Crooked executive-produced Dheezy Does It LP, which opens with an introduction from Eminem.
